response_schema.files: array of { id: string, name: string }

entries.scope_required: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly (or drive.metadata.readonly). drive.file only returns app-created files.
entries.notes: Drive API — added post-Gate-6 to let Get Document resolve a doc by name (the Docs API has no search/list). NOT yet validated live: the session token was documents-scope only and then expired (tokeninfo 400). Implementation follows the same Bearer-GET pattern as the validated calls. VALIDATE before shipping: run with a fresh drive.readonly token and confirm files[].id/name shape. Single quotes in the name are escaped (' -> \') for the Drive query language.

entries.scope_required: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file (already granted plugin-wide) — files created this way are 'app-created' so drive.file covers both this upload and the permissions.create call below.
entries.notes: Drive v3 simple multipart upload — used by GetImageUrlComponent to host a Bitmap or local File Path image so it has a URL the Docs API can fetch (insertInlineImage requires a publicly reachable URI, not a local path). Two-part multipart/related body: JSON metadata part ({name, mimeType}) + raw media part. .NET's MultipartContent("related") generates the boundary and Content-Type header automatically. NOT yet validated live — no Drive-scoped token available in the dev session. VALIDATE before shipping: run with a drive.file token and confirm the response.id shape.

Grants 'anyone with the link can view' on the file just uploaded by upload_image_to_drive — required because Docs API insertInlineImage fetches the image URI unauthenticated, so the Drive file must be link-public first. After this call, GetImageUrlComponent builds the fetchable URL as https://drive.google.com/uc?id={fileId} (the long-standing convention for embedding a public Drive file's raw bytes; Drive's own webContentLink triggers a download disposition instead). NOT yet validated live — same missing-token caveat as upload_image_to_drive.
